misconceptions.description: Writing a checklist row that asserts a result (the tool improved writing) without naming the artifact, source, or location that would let anyone verify it
misconceptions.trigger: row states a conclusion with no cited source or artifact
misconceptions.feedback: Name the artifact, where it lives, and the date range. A claim with no source is an opinion, not evidence.

misconceptions.description: Asserting improvement without a before measure, so there is nothing to compare the result against
misconceptions.trigger: row claims a gain but records no pre-tool baseline
misconceptions.feedback: Record the baseline. Improvement implies a before and an after measured the same way.

misconceptions.description: Gathering only evidence that supports the hoped-for conclusion and never looking for what would disconfirm it
misconceptions.trigger: row admits no possibility of being wrong and seeks no counter-case
misconceptions.feedback: State what would have changed your mind and whether you looked for it. Strong evidence can be disconfirmed.

misconceptions.description: Recording a result with no way for a colleague to re-check it, such as no stored artifacts or scoring method
misconceptions.trigger: row gives no path for an independent re-check
misconceptions.feedback: Make it verifiable: store the artifacts and name how a colleague could re-score or re-check the result.
